name: Matter
tagline: Save articles and newsletters into a clean reading queue with highlights and notes

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited read-later library and tags; full-text search; custom themes and fonts.

tiers.name: Matter Premium
tiers.limits: HD text-to-speech, AI Co-Reader, newsletters/RSS, unlimited highlights and notes, integrations and Kindle support.
tiers.notes: Current primary App Store annual SKU is $79.99/year.

pricing.freeTierCaps: unlimited read-later library and tags; full-text search; custom themes and fonts
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual through the App Store; auto-renews unless cancelled at least 24 hours before renewal
pricing.hiddenCosts: the App Store still lists legacy/alternate in-app-purchase SKUs, so existing subscribers or other storefront regions may see different amounts

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Matter, save articles and newsletters into a clean reading queue with highlights and notes. The hard boundary is email ingestion, mobile apps, text-to-speech, sync, and polished capture, plus capture polish, sync, and content partnerships.
coreLoopDIY: Save permitted articles, newsletters, and feeds into a clean reading queue, extract readable text, add highlights and notes, tag and search the archive, and export it in open formats.
whatYouLose: email ingestion, mobile apps, text-to-speech, sync, and polished capture
moatNotes: capture polish, sync, and content partnerships
ongoingBurden: feed quirks, parsing, paywalls, canonical URLs, deduplication, images, search, sync, browser extensions, and publisher changes
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Matter because people pay when capture works everywhere, reading state syncs instantly, and the archive remains clean without constant parser repairs. The recurring cost buys feed quirks, parsing, paywalls, canonical URLs, deduplication, images, search, sync, browser extensions, and publisher changes, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: FreshRSS
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source RSS reader with feeds, filters, and self-hosting support.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Folo
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Has RSS and one newsletter inbox, but no real highlight-and-note workflow for saved pages.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Karakeep
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Handles articles, RSS, highlights and notes, but it has no email-newsletter inbox.

rejectedAlternatives.name: NewsBlur
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Reads feeds and email newsletters, but does not replace Matter's page-highlighting workflow.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Matter Premium plan and a personal reading archive DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Matter in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, Readability.js, and a local background worker; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: save permitted articles, newsletters, and feeds into a clean reading queue, extract readable text, add highlights and notes, tag and search the archive, and export it in open formats.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Support manual URL save, RSS or Atom subscriptions, OPML import, and a simple bookmarklet.
Fetch politely with a clear user agent, rate limits, conditional requests, and robots-aware behavior.
Extract title, author, date, canonical URL, readable HTML, and selected images.
Provide inbox, unread, archive, favorites, tags, highlights, notes, and full-text search.
Keep the original URL prominent and never attempt to bypass authentication or paywalls.
Export OPML, bookmarks HTML, Markdown, and a complete JSON backup.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out paywall circumvention.
Deliberately leave out licensed publisher content and recommendation networks.
Deliberately leave out native mobile clients and seamless commercial sync.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
